newsitem.title: FRANCE: St-Gobain sees stable 1996 net result.
newsitem.headline: St-Gobain sees stable 1996 net result.

text.p: French building materials company Saint-Gobain expects to post 1996 net profits, excluding exceptional elements, similar to 1995, chairman Jean-Louis Beffa said on Friday.

"For 1996, the net attributable profit for the group, excluding all exceptional elements, should be of the same order of magnitude as last year, with a clear increase in cashflow," he told an analysts meeting.
The company posted 1995 net profit, excluding exceptionals, of 4.2 billion francs.

Beffa said the group had set short-term objectives for growth, profitability and return on investments. Although he gave no figure for growth targets, the firm aimed for a return on equity of more than 10 percent in net profit and minimum net cashflow of three percent, or more like four or five percent.
For Poliet, the firm it acquired this year, Beffa said he expected a "significant progress" in the second half over last year.

He added that he intended to retain Lapeyre, Poliet's subsidiary, withing the Saint-Gobain group. "I have no intention of spinning off Lapeyre...I will show that it is profitable for Saint-Gobain's shareholders," he said.
On the economic climate, he said the most likely outlook was for a slightly easing domestic gloom in the second half and a pickup in consumption in the period.
